title: Food hygiene essentials
siteNotes: Where the handwash basins, sanitiser and colour-coded boards and cloths are kept, and the colour code in use
The venue's cleaning chemicals, contact times and the cleaning schedule
Who to tell when you are unwell (name and phone number), and the fitness-to-work return form if one is used
The venue's pest control contractor and where pest sightings are logged
Where delivery checks are recorded, and who can accept or reject a delivery
The venue's own fridge limit if stricter than 8C
legalNotes: Staff must be supervised, instructed or trained in food hygiene to suit their work: Regulation (EC) 852/2004 Annex II ch. XII, as it applies in England; Food Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013. https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/2996

Handwashing, clean work clothing and reporting illness: Regulation 852/2004 Annex II ch. VIII (personal hygiene). People likely to contaminate food must not handle it, and must report illness or symptoms to the business immediately.

48 hours: FSA fitness-to-work guidance says staff with diarrhoea or vomiting should normally be excluded from open food until 48 hours after symptoms stop naturally. Reportable symptoms also include fever, jaundice, infected skin, and diarrhoea or vomiting in the household. Source: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fitness-to-work/fitness-to-work. Verified.

Chilled food must be kept at 8C or below by law; 5C or below is the FSA's recommended target. Source: Food Hygiene (England) Regulations 2013 and FSA Safer food, better business (https://www.food.gov.uk/business-guidance/sfbb). Confirmed by secondary sources; the FSA page itself could not be fetched.

Cross-contamination, cleaning and disinfecting, and pest control: Regulation 852/2004 Annex II ch. I, V and IX, and SFBB. Cleaning removes dirt; disinfecting kills bacteria, with a contact time set by the product label.
Not verified directly: exact handwashing duration. 'About 20 seconds' is common NHS and FSA-aligned training advice, not a legal requirement.
Not verified directly from the FSA site (pages unavailable when checked): specific delivery checks. The general rule (chilled at 8C or below, frozen hard, packaging intact, in date) follows SFBB.

Review Oct 2026: 48-hour exclusion and the 8C legal limit / 5C recommended confirmed as stated (8C limit has exceptions such as short periods during service, not taught). Slide 5 changed: 'rinse' is not always needed; many sanitisers are no-rinse, so follow the label. Check 11 option A changed from 'feels cold' to 'is cold': a delivery's temperature should be judged with a probe thermometer, not by touch. Handwashing time of about 20 seconds is NHS-style training advice, not law. Level 2 certificate is good practice, not a legal requirement.

cards.kicker: Kitchen, front of house and bar · 14 minutes
cards.title: Food hygiene essentials
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- wash your hands properly and know when you must not work
- stop germs spreading from raw food, hands and surfaces
- keep food safe from delivery to plate

cards.title: Clean hands, every time
cards.body:
Hands move germs more than anything else in a kitchen. Use the handwash basin, not the sink you prepare food in. Wash for about 20 seconds with soap and warm water, then dry on paper towel.

Your manager will show you where the basins are.

cards.title: When to wash
cards.body: Wash before you start work and any time your hands could have picked something up. A quick rinse is not enough.

items: Before starting or returning to the kitchen
After touching raw meat, fish, eggs or veg
After coughing, sneezing or touching your face
After handling money or your phone

cards.title: Unwell? Tell us first
cards.body:
If you have diarrhoea or vomiting, do not handle food. Tell your manager straight away. You should normally stay away from open food until **48 hours after your symptoms stop**. Report sickness, fever, a yellow tinge to your skin, infected cuts or sores, and tummy bugs at home too.

> Nobody will be in trouble for telling us. Working ill is what puts guests at risk.

left.title: Do
items: Cover cuts with a waterproof plaster

right.title: Do not
items: Come in and hope no one notices
Return the day you feel better
Wait for the end of the shift to say

cards.title: Keep raw and ready-to-eat apart
cards.body: Raw meat, fish, eggs and unwashed veg carry bacteria that cooking kills but a salad does not. Contamination happens through hands, boards, knives, cloths, fridge shelves and drips. Your manager will show you the colour-coded boards and where each food lives.

items.title: Separate kit
items.text: Raw and cooked use different boards and knives

items.title: Fridge order
items.text: Ready-to-eat on top, raw meat at the bottom

items.title: Cloths
items.text: Never wipe raw then ready-to-eat with one cloth

cards.title: Clean first, then disinfect
cards.body: Disinfectant cannot work through grease and food. Clean off the dirt with hot water and detergent, then use a disinfectant or sanitiser, leaving it on for the **contact time on the label**. Rinse if the label says to, then dry. Your manager will show you the products and the cleaning schedule.

items.title: Rinse if needed
items.text: Follow the label, then air dry

cards.title: Safe from the van to the shelf
cards.body:
Check every delivery before you sign: chilled food cold, frozen food hard, packaging undamaged, dates in. Put chilled food away first. Chilled food must be kept at **8°C or below by law**; 5°C or below is the recommended target. Cover and label food, and bin anything out of date. Report droppings, gnawing or flies to your manager.

Your manager will show you where deliveries are recorded.

items.title: Report pests
items.text: Droppings, gnawing, flies: tell a manager

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Wash your hands properly, often, at the handwash basin.
- Diarrhoea or vomiting: do not handle food, tell your manager, and stay off until 48 hours after it stops.
- Keep raw and ready-to-eat food, boards and cloths apart.
- Clean first, then disinfect for the label's contact time.
- Check deliveries and keep chilled food at 8°C or below (aim for 5°C).

cards.q: Mo had a stomach bug and was sick last night. He feels fine this morning and is rostered on the pass. What should happen?
options: He works but only on cooked food and salads
He wears gloves and washes his hands often
He tells his manager and stays off food for 48 hours clear
He works a short shift and sees how he feels
cards.why: People can carry the bug for a couple of days after they feel better. Staff should normally stay away from open food until 48 hours after symptoms stop naturally.

cards.q: Gloves mean you do not need to wash your hands as often.
cards.why: Gloves pick up germs just like hands. Wash your hands and change gloves between tasks, especially after raw food.

cards.q: You wiped a greasy prep surface with sanitiser straight away and it looks clean. What is wrong with that?
options: Nothing, sanitiser both cleans and kills germs in one go
Sanitiser should always be rinsed off straight away
Surfaces should be dried at once with a tea towel
It needed detergent first, then sanitiser left for its contact time
cards.why: Dirt and grease stop disinfectant working. Clean first, then disinfect and leave it for the contact time on the label.

cards.q: Which TWO of these must you do on a chilled delivery?
options: Check it is cold and the packaging is undamaged
Sign for it first and check later
Check the dates and put chilled food away promptly
Leave it on the back step until the chef is free
Stack it on the floor of the walk-in
cards.why: Check before you sign, and get chilled food into the fridge quickly. Leaving it out lets it warm up.

cards.q: Where should raw chicken go in the fridge?
options: On the top shelf, so it is easy to reach
On the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food
Beside the salads, in a sealed bag
Wherever there is space
cards.why: Raw meat can drip. Keeping it on the bottom shelf stops juices landing on food that will not be cooked.

cards.q: You have just handled raw chicken. What must you do before slicing tomatoes?
options: Wipe your hands on a clean apron
Rinse them quickly in the prep sink
Pull a fresh glove on over the top
Wash them at the handwash basin
cards.why: Raw chicken leaves bacteria on your hands that tomatoes will not kill. Wash with soap and warm water at the handwash basin, then dry on paper towel.

cards.q: A housemate has had diarrhoea and vomiting but you feel fine, so you do not need to mention it at work.
cards.why: Illness at home is something to report to your manager before you handle food, because you could be carrying it.

cards.q: You find mouse droppings behind the dry store shelves. What do you do?
options: Sweep them up and carry on
Tell your manager straight away
Set a trap from the shop yourself
Cover them over and finish your job
cards.why: Signs of pests must be reported so they can be dealt with properly. Do not clear them up and say nothing.

cards.q: A couple of seconds under the tap with soap is enough to wash your hands.
cards.why: Wash for about 20 seconds, covering palms, backs, thumbs and between fingers, then dry on paper towel.

cards.q: Which TWO are times you must wash your hands?
options: After taking out the bins
When you swap from one glass to another
After coughing or touching your face
Before putting your own coat on
After checking the rota
cards.why: Bins, coughing and touching your face all put germs on your hands. Wash after each before touching food.
